title: Double treble (UK)
subtitle: UK double treble equals US treble crochet — the tallest of the standard stitches
excerpt: The double treble is the tallest common stitch: yarn over twice before entering the stitch, then close down in three stages. Used where you need open, lacy fabric or a long raised post — filet crochet, shells, long bobbles.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet chapter — the long treble family. Weldon's Practical Crochet series.

glossaryTerms.definition: Abbreviation for double treble in UK crochet patterns. The equivalent US stitch is the treble crochet, abbreviated tr in US patterns.
The vertical column of yarn that forms the body of a treble-family stitch between the base and the top V. The post is what is worked around when making post stitches.

heroPrompt: A swatch of double treble stitches in pale blue DK yarn on a white background — the tall open stitches showing clear V-tops and long posts, about 6 stitches wide and 3 rows deep.

content.text: The double treble is the tallest of the standard crochet stitches. Abbreviated
in UK patterns — the same stitch is called treble crochet (tr) in US patterns. A UK double treble stands roughly 15 mm tall in DK yarn at a 4 mm hook. The tall
creates open, airy fabric: the right choice for filet crochet mesh, lacy shawl structures, and shell patterns.

attrs.title: Terminology reminder
attrs.body: UK dtr = US tr (treble crochet). UK treble (tr) = US double crochet (dc). These are the two most confusing mismatches. If you are working a US pattern that says 'tr', it means the stitch that UK patterns call double treble — two yarn overs at the start, three close-down stages.

content.text: Yarn over twice (two wraps before entering the stitch). You now have three loops on the hook.
Insert the hook into the stitch. Yarn over and pull a loop through. Four loops on the hook.
Yarn over and pull through the first two loops on the hook. Three loops remain.
Yarn over and pull through the next two loops. Two loops remain.
Yarn over and pull through the last two loops. One loop remains on the hook. The double treble is complete.
Turning chain for the double treble row

A row of double trebles needs a 4-chain turning chain at the start of each row. The turning chain counts as the first double treble of the row in most patterns (this is the default — check the pattern notes if not specified). Work the next stitch into the second stitch of the previous row, not the first, because the turning chain has taken the first position. At the end of the row, the last dtr of the new row enters the top of the 4-chain turning chain from the row below.

Double crochet (UK): 0 starting yarn overs, closes in 1 stage. Half treble: 1 starting yarn over, closes in 1 stage over 3 loops. Treble: 1 starting yarn over, closes in 2 stages. Double treble: 2 starting yarn overs, closes in 3 stages. Each extra starting yarn over adds roughly 3-4 mm of height and one extra close-down step. Triple treble (ttr) — 3 starting yarn overs, closes in 4 stages — appears in some lace and Tunisian patterns.

attrs.heading: Double treble problems
attrs.intro: Two common issues when learning the double treble.

items.symptom: The stitch leans and won't stand up straight
items.cause: The two starting yarn overs are not evenly tensioned, so one pulls tighter than the other as you close down.
items.fix: Keep the tension hand active throughout the close-down. After each pull-through, gently tug the working yarn to seat the loop before the next yarn over.

items.symptom: Stitches at the end of the row are shorter than the rest
items.cause: The turning chain is being skipped or the last stitch is worked into the wrong post.
items.fix: Count the turning chain as the first dtr and enter the top of it at the end of the following row. If the row count still drops, mark the top of the turning chain with a stitch marker at the turn.
